subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw support a secure cross-machine Chrome extension relay again, and if so should it be a first-party browser driver or a plugin/backend API implementation?
rationale: The issue is valid at source level, but the fix crosses browser-control security boundaries and public config/plugin API design, so automation should not choose between restoring the old relay, building a new backend seam, or keeping the relay retired.

options.title: Design secure backend seam
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved browser backend/plugin API and implement the relay as an optional vetted backend with scoped permissions, audit logs, migration, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Close or narrow the request after documenting that managed-hosting users must use node hosts, remote CDP, or an external relay outside OpenClaw core.

options.title: Restore first-party relay
options.body: Bring back the legacy extension relay as a built-in driver, accepting the compatibility benefit and owning the renewed security and maintenance surface in core.

recommendation.title: Design secure backend seam
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved browser backend/plugin API and implement the relay as an optional vetted backend with scoped permissions, audit logs, migration, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest recent merged history for the relay removal and existing-session migration surface.
